source_quote: DC-to-DC buck and boost converters; and applications of DIAC, TRIAC, and IGBT.
answer: ELEC 432L Power Electronics Lab: rectifiers with diodes and thyristors, DC-to-AC converters, buck and boost converters, and DIAC, TRIAC and IGBT applications. Co-requisite: ELEC 432.

source_quote: This course is to explore the modeling of linear dynamic systems via differential
answer: ELEC 451 Control Systems, 3(3,0): modeling linear dynamic systems (state-space and transfer functions), time and frequency domain analysis, Routh-Hurwitz and Nyquist stability, root locus and Bode design, PID and lead/lag control. Prerequisite: CCEE 331.

source_quote: This Co-op work experience is designed to provide students with 5 weeks of short-
answer: ELEC 499 Co-op Work Experience, 3(3,0): short-term work in electrical engineering with a report, poster and PowerPoint presentation. The description states 5 weeks. Prerequisites: ENGL 217; Senior Standing.
review_note: Description (p.316) says 5 weeks, while the program Co-op section (p.307) and the university Co-op policy require 8 weeks.

source_quote: This course focuses on the basic structure and principles of DC and AC drive systems.
answer: ELEC 533 Advanced Electric Machines and Drives, 3(3,0): DC and AC drives, field weakening, constant torque/hp operation, space vectors, PWM, multi-level converters, field-oriented and direct torque control, and sensorless control. Prerequisites: ELEC 331 and ELEC 432.

source_quote: analysis by covering the following topics: Circuit models, Per-unit representation,
answer: ELEC 534 Advanced Power Systems, 3(3,0): circuit models, per-unit, network methods, load-flow studies and control, economic dispatch, symmetrical and unsymmetrical faults, stability and computer methods. Prerequisite: ELEC 330.

source_quote: The first phase of a team-oriented, project-based experience that culminates in the
answer: ELEC 595A (1(1,0), prerequisite ENGL 217) and ELEC 595B (3(3,0), prerequisite ELEC 595A) are the two phases of the BE Summative Learning Project: a team project creating an artifact with proposal, creative solution, report, presentation and demonstration.

source_quote: This course introduces high-voltage engineering, withstand levels, S curves, insulation
answer: ELEC 433 High Voltage Engineering, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: withstand levels, insulation coordination, breakdown, non-destructive testing, partial discharge, over-voltages, lightning and protection devices. Prerequisite: ELEC 330.

source_quote: This course covers general considerations; load characteristics; sub-transmission and
answer: ELEC 434 Electrical Power Distribution, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: load characteristics, substations, primary and secondary distribution, transformers, voltage regulation, capacitors and protective device coordination. Prerequisite: ELEC 330.

source_quote: This course introduces Electromagnetic Interference, Conducted and Radiated
answer: ELEC 444 Electromagnetic Compatibility, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: EMI, conducted and radiated emission and susceptibility, EMC standards, design and test facilities. Prerequisite: ELEC 210.

source_quote: carefully selected from ELEC-related areas. The contents of such a course are to be
answer: ELEC 498 Special Topics in Electrical Engineering, 3(3,0): current special topics selected by the instructor and department (instructor's consent per elective table).

source_quote: This course focuses on the foundations of neural network theory and its application in
answer: ELEC 503 Artificial Neural Systems, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: neural network theory, supervised and unsupervised learning, feed-forward and recurrent networks, perceptron layers, associative memories and feature maps. Prerequisite: MATH 311.

source_quote: This course is designed to give students a functional knowledge of lasers. The course
answer: ELEC 504 Lasers and Laser Applications in Engineering, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: light, atoms, absorption and stimulated emission, laser types, resonators and amplifiers, and engineering and biomedical applications. No prerequisite is listed.

source_quote: on the equipment needed to support new forms of electric transportation, such as
answer: ELEC 531 Electrical Power Systems for Transportation Applications, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: power systems and control equipment for electric cars, aircraft and trains. Prerequisite: ELEC 432.

source_quote: covering the following topics: Flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS), conventional
answer: ELEC 532 Application of Power Electronics in Power Systems, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: FACTS, thyristor-controlled reactors, phase shifters, STATCON and UPFC. Prerequisites: ELEC 330 and ELEC 432.

source_quote: This course covers Energy and carbon emissions in the built environment, including
answer: ELEC 535 Renewable Energy Systems for the Built Environment, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: energy and carbon in buildings including Lebanese data, building services (HVAC, lighting, hot water, lifts), consumption benchmarks and the Lean-Clean-Green principle. Prerequisite: ELEC 210.

source_quote: This course aims to provide knowledge about energy production from renewable
answer: ELEC 536 Renewable Energy Systems, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: renewable generation, interconnected grids, electricity markets and policy, wind conversion, microgrids, and modeling and control of wind, solar, fuel cells and power electronics interfaces. Prerequisite: ELEC 431.

source_quote: switching power converters, advanced power converter topologies, design constraints,
answer: ELEC 542 Advanced Power Electronics, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: modeling switching converters, advanced topologies, design constraints, control, multi-level inverters and matrix converters. Prerequisite: ELEC 432.

source_quote: This course focuses on the formulation of the linear control problem using state-space
answer: ELEC 550 Advanced Control Systems, 3(3,0): state-space control, frequency and time response, controllability, observability, canonical forms, state transition matrices, stability, linearization and discrete systems. Prerequisite: ELEC 451.

source_quote: This course presents a comprehensive exposition of the theory of nonlinear dynamical
answer: ELEC 551 Nonlinear Adaptive Control, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: nonlinear dynamical systems theory and controller design for nonlinear systems. Prerequisite: ELEC 451.

source_quote: and policy choices regarding energy generation and use. We will focus equally on the
answer: ELEC 560 Sustainable Energy, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: technical, economic, political and environmental aspects of energy generation and use. The description lists ELEC 431 as prerequisite.
review_note: Elective table (p.306) lists the prerequisite as None; description (p.319) lists ELEC 431.

source_quote: This course aims to provide the students with an in-depth understanding of the
answer: ELEC 561 Wind Energy Technology, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: wind turbine types, power output estimation, tower structural suitability, and onshore/offshore wind systems. The description lists ELEC 210 as prerequisite.
review_note: Elective table (p.306) lists ELEC 431 and ELEC 432; description (p.319) lists ELEC 210.

source_quote: This course aims to provide students with a systematic understanding of current
answer: ELEC 562 Solar Energy Technology, 3(3,0), an electrical technical elective: solar photovoltaic technologies, current research and advances, and assessing PV technologies. Prerequisite: ELEC 210.

answer: ELEC 597 Advanced Topics in Electrical Engineering, 3(3,0): a specific advanced topic defined by the instructor and approved by the chair; offered on demand. Prerequisite: instructor's consent.
